key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving electronic uniformity, showing that morphology and optoelectronic quality can be decoupled.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route toward durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother film surfaces.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium on 3D perovskites.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative QFLS, retaining optoelectronic homogeneity better than pristine films during accelerated aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device-level efficiency or operational lifetime, so photovoltaic performance gains remain to be established.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
